endorsements.quote: Approval from the ethics committee or institutional review board must be secured to ensure compliance with ethical standards.
After training the LLM on refined data and developing the user interface/integration with EHR, pilot testing with a small patient cohort under clinical oversight should be initiated.
Regular audits, including external audits by independent bodies, help maintain compliance with regulatory requirements post-deployment.
Training gastroenterologists on LLMs ensures safe and effective integration into clinical workflows.
Data must be adequate and representative of the intended population, as models fine-tuned on specific demographic groups may underperform in others.

To mitigate bias, strategies like re-weighting underrepresented patient populations in training data or supplementing the model with diverse clinical trial data can help ensure fairer recommendations.
Adherence to the HIPAA in the United States and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in Europe is essential.

Key preprocessing steps involve structured (e.g., HCV RNA levels, fibrosis scores) and unstructured data (e.g., clinical notes describing symptoms or treatment history) integration while ensuring Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)-compliant de-identification.
Cross-referencing outputs from trusted guidelines and developing internal layers that detect unsupported outputs can prevent hallucinations.
Model calibration adjusts confidence scores to prevent overconfidence in uncertain cases, helping clinicians gauge trust in recommendations.
Transparent patient communication about AI’s role reinforces that LLMs support, rather than replace, clinical judgment.

unlisted_practices: Assemble a multidisciplinary team of AI specialists, clinicians, bioethicists, and regulatory experts to develop clinical LLMs.
Use active learning and reinforcement learning from human feedback to continuously improve deployed LLMs using clinician feedback.
Use out-of-distribution detection so the model flags cases outside its training data and prompts clinicians to seek expert input.
Use structured prompts, controlled vocabulary, and response formatting constraints to reduce LLM output variability.
Validate LLM output variability through inter-clinician agreement studies and comparison with clinical decision support systems.
Evaluate LLM treatment recommendations on relevance, coherence, and safety, and monitor clinical outcomes such as cure rates and adherence.
Disseminate AI model findings through peer-reviewed publications and share code and data to promote transparency and reproducibility.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework and commentary article proposing guidelines and structured steps for deploying and safeguarding large language models in gastroenterology.
